The introduction of branched alklyl chains to oligothiophenes improves the solubilities of the compounds without sacrificing the electrical properties of the resulting thin-film transistors.

1) the introduction of branched alkly chains into the oligothiophene derivatives leads to a drastic increase in solubility, while the charge carrier mobility remains high; and 2) the introduction of the branched alkyl groups into the sexithiophenyl unit results in an increase in solubilizing power, while the mobility of the charge carriers is not affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel oligo(thiophene)s with improved solubility.
the development of solution-processable organic semiconductors for use in thin-film transistor devices and the study of the effects of the chemical structure on the electronic properties.
the design and synthesis of new solution-processable oligothiophene derivatives with branched alkyl side chains.
